Location: Primarily Stora Skedvi alternatively Storvik. Your application is welcome! For more information: Business area manager: Ylva Azcarate 0730-39 14 25 Subject area manager: Line Strand 070-207 33 07 Union contact person: Ylva Andersson 073-336 76 69 The service is a permanent full-time employment. The workplace is covered by a collective agreement. We want applications with a personal letter and CV no later than January 31, 2025. Interviews will take place continuously and employment may become available before the end of the application period. HS Konsult AB sells independent advice to agricultural companies in Uppsala, Stockholm, Södermanland, Västmanland, Örebro, Gävleborg and Dalarna counties. We are 60 employees at the offices in Uppsala, Nyköping, Strängnäs, Örebro, Västerås, Storvik, Stora Skedvi and Bollnäs. Based on our shared value base based on competence, reliability and trust, we work together for development and increased profitability within the green industries.

From our base in Skåne, we raise and sell breeding chickens to customers in Sweden and the Nordics. We supply our customers with traditionally white-feathered breeding chickens but also chickens that are slow-growing or brown-feathered. We are a company that is proud of agriculture and food production, with a company management that prioritizes teamwork and drives innovation and development to always do the best for our animals, our customers and for our employees. The responsibility that comes with the position is to follow the company's policies and values, as well as responsibility for all processes within production and act to ensure these:• Animal care responsibility • Quality responsibility • Strive for improvement and set goals Due to the risk of infection, you cannot hold or have regular contact with birds, pigs or reptiles. id: 1824076
title: Vi söker växtodlingsrådgivare till växtskyddscentralen i Landskrona
description: The Swedish Agency for Agriculture exists to promote increased and sustainable food production and good animal welfare throughout Sweden. We contribute to a living countryside. About 1,850 people work with us. The head office is in Jönköping, but we also have large regional operations. We work actively to ensure that our employees are sustainable and happy at work! We invest long-term in our employees and want them to develop together with us! We offer a good working environment with generous benefits with up to 35 vacation days, wellness allowance and wellness time. In a large part of our employment, we offer flexible working hours, the possibility to work mobile and to work parts of the working time remotely. Read more about what it is like to work at the Swedish Agricultural Agency on our website: www.jordbruksverket.se/jobbahosossARBETSUPPGIFTERWe are looking for two crop cultivation advisors to The Swedish Agricultural Agency's plant protection centers in Landskrona. For the first position, we are looking for someone who has a few years' experience as a consultant and wants to take responsibility, influence and plan the operations for the Plant Protection Center in Landskrona. For the second position, we are looking for you who want to develop your skills as an advisor, work in the field and take responsibility for diagnoses connected to lab operations. For both positions, this means that you actively influence and contribute to how we achieve our goals with an integrated plant protection and a competitive, profitable and increasing food production. You will collaborate and exchange experiences with colleagues at other plant protection centers as well as with colleagues at other units within the Swedish Agency for Agriculture. Your main task is to support the existing advice with basis built on a scientific basis. You contribute to the development of integrated plant protection through independent advice and basis for need-based control. The services include, among other things:• Compiling and conveying Swedish and international experiences and results in the field of plant protection to the consultancy • Follow the development of plant pests during the season within the Swedish Agency for Agriculture's forecasting activities for various pests, as well as participate in digital weekly meetings for advisors about the current plant protection situation • Contribute to increased awareness of difficult-to-control weeds and spread knowledge about sustainable cultivation systems The work involves many contacts, mainly national but also some international. Within the Environment and Climate Knowledge Hub, which includes the plant protection centre, we work in teams and help each other with the tasks that need to be carried out. This means that you can also have the opportunity to work with other tasks in the field of plant protection. This could be, for example, participating in investigations, contingency planning or issues related to the ongoing climate change. You should therefore be able to manage a flexible way of working and be able to quickly adapt to changed tasks based on new priorities. QUALIFICATIONS Common to the two positions is that we are looking for you who are an agronomist with a focus on soil/plants, horticulturist, farm manager or have equivalent education. You have good knowledge of plant pests and integrated plant protection in agricultural crops and are well acquainted with the conditions for agriculture in Sweden. The work is about supporting the counseling by acquiring and conveying knowledge. It is therefore important that you have the ability to collaborate and communicate in a clear and professional manner in order to get your message across. In order to achieve success, good knowledge of Swedish and English, both spoken and written, is a prerequisite. For the first position, we also want you to have a few years' experience of working as a plant breeding advisor under Nordic conditions. You are stable in your role as an advisor and can handle stress in a constructive way. Environmental monitoring in the field of plant protection is also an important part of the work. For the second position, you are required to have experience and interest in working in a lab and knowledge of diagnostics for fungi and insects. You should be structured and be able to find solutions to problems that arise. The job includes some travel and a driver's license is a requirement for both positions. OTHER Location is Landskrona, alternatively Skara with the possibility to work some parts remotely. on the labor market are taken care of. We welcome all applicants and strive for diversity. We normally apply a 6-month trial period. Before the recruitment work, we have taken a position on recruitment channels and marketing. We therefore do not want to be contacted by advertising vendors or recruitment companies.

id: 1705490
title: Work with plant protection - three services in our socially important business
description: The Swedish Agency for Agriculture exists to promote increased and sustainable food production and good animal welfare throughout Sweden. We contribute to a living countryside. About 1,750 people work with us. The head office is in Jönköping, but we also have large regional operations. Read more about what it's like to work at Jordbruksverket on our website: www. the agricultural agency. se/jobbahososs As an advisor in plant protection, you will be part of the plant protection center in Skara, which is part of the environment and climate knowledge hub and works to actively influence and contribute to sustainable plant protection and a competitive, profitable and increased food production. We work in teams and help each other with the tasks that need to be carried out. The colleagues in the environment and climate knowledge hub are mainly located regionally at the Swedish Agency for Agriculture's three advisory units. This position is located at the plant protection advisory unit, which includes the plant protection centre. At the plant control unit, where the administrative positions are located, we are responsible for managing, among other things the rules for seed and against plant pests. This means everything from EU and international work, to national regulations and decisions, together with a lot of guidance, information and preparedness work. At the unit, we are 18 employees divided into two teams. We work both directly with industry players, industry organizations and in collaboration with the government office and other member states. JOB TASKS Do you have a good knowledge of the challenges of plant cultivation and want to work for robust and sustainable plant protection? Do you want to contribute to us being able to continue growing crops for feed and food in Sweden even in the event of social disturbances and in a changed climate? Then you can become one of our new colleagues! The Swedish Agency for Agriculture has an important task in both working with preventive plant protection and combating plant pests that are already present here, partly through regulations and partly through advice and skills development. We are now advertising three positions with the following tasks: 1. Advisor crop protection, agriculture - Skara• compile and convey Swedish and international experiences and results in the field of plant protection to the consultancy, • support the consultancy with increased competence through newsletters, control recommendations, courses, field trips and conferences, • follow the development of plant pests during the season within the Swedish Agency for Agriculture's forecasting activities for various pests, • increase awareness of difficult-to-control weeds and spread knowledge about sustainable cultivation systems, • be an important part of various projects within preparedness to ensure that we can maintain Swedish food production2. Plant pest manager - Jönköping/Landskrona• guide and inform about our rules against quarantine pests, • strengthen our preparedness for and manage possible outbreaks, • contribute to planning and developing our inventory of quarantine pests. Together with the colleagues at the plant regulation unit, you protect Sweden against the introduction of new plant pests. The work involves a mixture of situations that requires quick responses and planned work with processes based on scouting and reflection. 3. Manager robust crop cultivation - Jönköping• what abilities are needed to run the business, • what vulnerabilities exist and • what we need to do to increase our ability. Together with colleagues, you contribute to making our socially important business more robust with rules and guidance both on seed and combating plant pests. This is to reduce our vulnerability and strengthen our preparedness to face new as well as ongoing challenges. QUALIFICATIONSWe are looking for you who have an academic education as an agronomist, hortologist, farm manager, horticultural engineer or equivalent and a good knowledge of crop cultivation in Sweden. You need a good ability to express yourself verbally and in writing, in both Swedish and English to be successful in the role of administrator or advisor. The roles have different qualifying requirements, where the personal abilities we are looking for may differ, depending on the nature of the role and task. The following paragraphs clarify which requirements are specifically aimed at a particular service. 1. For advisers in crop protection, in addition to the requirements above, you need to have experience of working as a plant cultivation adviser under Nordic conditions and good knowledge of plant pests and integrated plant protection in agricultural crops. You are structured and used to planning your work, are confident in your professional role and find solutions to get ahead even in uncertain contexts. You stay up-to-date by monitoring the world around you and find it easy to put forward your case and win respect. 2. For plant pest manager, you need to be structured, analytical and communicative. It is advantageous to have knowledge of plant pests, gardening, plant cultivation or forests in Nordic conditions, and if you have experience of government work. 3. For manager of robust crop cultivation, we are looking for you who is structured, stable and has an easy time collaborating and communicating with others, both customers and other actors. You have previous experience of government work and we would like you to have experience of work in civil defence. OTHER Location of the services is presented below:1. Plant protection advisers are primarily located in Skara, but Linköping can also be an option. 2. Pest control officers are based in Jönköping or Landskrona. 3. Handler robust crop cultivation is located in Jönköping. For all three positions, the opportunity to work part of the working time remotely is offered. Do you have questions about any of the services? 1. For plant protection advisers, contact Anna Larsson or Anders Arvidsson. 2. For plant pest managers, contact Carin Bunnvik. 3. For managers robust plant cultivation, contact Carin Bunnvik or Klara Ekengard. For us, it is important that all skills in the labor market are utilized. We welcome all applicants and strive for diversity. We normally apply a 6-month trial period. Before the recruitment work, we have taken a position on recruitment channels and marketing. We therefore do not want to be contacted by advertising vendors or recruitment companies.

description: Farmers - Farmer's description Hälsingegården & Hälsingland Lammkvalité is a smaller agriculture in the village Långhed CA6 km from Alfta along the Tourist Road Stora Hälsingegårdars väg. We who live on the farm are now pensioners and work voluntarily with the aim of preserving highly endangered land breeds, a unique cultural landscape and elderly buildings in consultation with, among other things. country associations, Swedish Agricultural Agency, Swedish cultural landscape and Gävleborgsfäbodförening. In the yard there is also a summer café and a smaller building maintenance shop. The yard is originally from the 19th century and consists of a single-modern manor building, older K-labeled Gammelgård, economy buildings and an architectural sheep house with plumbing rooms, living rooms and chicken houses. In the older barn there is room for 7fjällnära cows. In the yard there are also 15 helsing sheep, Gotland rabbits, cats and dogs. We who live in the farm are the writers and agricultural historians. The farm is run as a simpler self -catering with land and animal care, vegetable cultivation and cultural tourism in relation to the Hälsingegårdarna such as UNESCO World Heritage in traditionally distinct cultural environment. The work is of a practical distance and is varied. You should be healthy and strong and have knowledge of traditional bond knowledge. A dream job for the right person.The quality you should be energetic, have common sense and be able to work independently and effectively in a small vulnerable business where we must have confidence in each other. You should have good experience in small -scale agriculture, preferably ecological focus. You should have good knowledge of ice-scale older soil management and cultivation. testCases.name: test_case_16
testCases.input: Are there any positions available for professionals involved in agricultural policy development and implementation?
testCases.actualOutput:
Yes, the provided database contains several positions relevant to agricultural policy development and implementation. Here are the available roles:

*   **Administrators and advisors with a focus on farm animals**
    *   **Description:** This role involves working at the regional government level to ensure national political goals for agriculture have an impact. Responsibilities include planning and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy (advice, courses, and information), managing project and investment support, handling land acquisition permits, and participating in cross-sectoral groups to contribute an agricultural perspective on various policy issues.

*   **Responsable de pôle installation en agriculture (F/H)**
    *   **Description:** This position involves managing regional policy regarding the installation of new farmers to ensure generational renewal. Key duties include designing, implementing, and monitoring regional installation policies, providing technical-economic expertise on support files, and coordinating with European programs (such as FEADER/EAFRD) to modernize and simplify aid systems.

*   **Substitute Cultivation coordinator/project manager**
    *   **Description:** This role focuses on implementing a municipality-wide cultivation strategy and action plan. Responsibilities include integrating cultivation into community planning, supporting professional horticulture and agriculture, and developing systems for cultivation advice and grants to achieve sustainability goals.

*   **Agricultural adviser to the Councilors in Sjuhärad**
    *   **Description:** This role provides advisory services to farms and includes opportunities to work on various projects connected to agriculture, involving collaboration with organizations that carry out research and training activities.

*   **Agronomists or Land Managers (Agricultural Economic Survey)**
    *   **Description:** These roles involve working on an agricultural economic survey used to model, investigate, and evaluate the common agricultural policy. Responsibilities include collecting data, analyzing agricultural companies from a holistic perspective, and producing statistics and feedback reports for the European Commission and other stakeholders.

*   **Work with plant protection (Three services)**
    *   **Description:** These roles include an "Advisor crop protection," "Plant pest manager," and "Manager robust crop cultivation." These positions involve managing national regulations, EU and international work, and providing guidance and information to ensure sustainable plant protection and robust food production.

job_description: The county board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for the agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sector collaboration at the County Board. We work with experts in these fields who are happy to share their knowledge. We work with respect, professionalism and openness for the county's residents - together for a sustainable future! The county. This includes, among other things, counseling and skills-enhancing activities aimed at the county's farmers. Our current pet consultant is now retiring and we are therefore looking for her successor who wants to work with skills development for the county's farmers with a focus on the farm's animal husbandry. Job duties You will be part of a group that works with planning, implementing and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy in the form of advice, courses and information to farmers. The work entails partly independently carrying out competence-enhancing initiatives such as courses, counseling and farm meetings with exchange of experience and partly coordinating other actors that the county administrative board has procured for various activities. You write applications for project funds and, together with colleagues, carry out the procurement of competence development efforts. The work includes financial accounting and reporting of measures taken. You collaborate with industry actors and organizations and have close cooperation with other county administrative boards as well as with various functions at our county administrative board. You may be part of cross-sectoral groups where you need to be able to combine your expertise with a holistic perspective. You participate in the work of responding to referrals and contributing with the perspective of agriculture on various issues. Depending on experience and competence, other tasks at the unit may also be part of the position. Your work is independent and requires you to be self-motivated, results-oriented and good at collaborating and creating relationships. You are sensitive to the needs of different clients. In your dialogue with farmers, you need to be service-oriented and have a good understanding of the companies' conditions in the county and have the ability to see the whole. You have a few years of work experience, experience from consultancy and government work is advantageous. You have work experience with a focus on agriculture and farm animals. If you also have experience in project management and work with skills development, as well as experience in working with small business owners, this is advantageous. You have the ability to communicate clearly in both speech and writing and have an established network within the agricultural industry. You are structured and solution-oriented with good computer skills. The position involves travel, mainly in the county, but longer trips with overnight stays also occur. A driver's license for a passenger car is required. We offer you meaningful work with varied tasks. You will make a difference to our county and society. The County Board is a broad authority, which means that you constantly have the opportunity to develop and learn new things. This applies in several policy areas. As an employer, we have a strong focus on good employment conditions, active work environment work and health-promoting wellness activities. We are keen on cooperation with our union partners and can offer remote work. In case of permanent employment at the County Board, you will be placed at war with the authority. job_title: Agricultural adviser to the Councilors in Sjuhärad
job_description: Do you want to work with cattle and crop production? Advise on feed for milk and meat production from sowing to feed table? Then this could be something for you! About the service The service is a unique combination of crop cultivation, mainly fodder, and advisory services to farms with milk or meat production. You will be part of working groups with pet advisors and crop advisors. There is also the opportunity to work in various projects connected to agriculture. About you We are looking for you who are agronomists, land managers or have equivalent education. You must have experience in both crop cultivation and cattle. You need to enjoy having customer contact and like working in a team. Great emphasis is placed on personal suitability. We offer We have a wide range of activities in finance, crop cultivation, forestry and animal production. The advisers also have a department with pet technicians who perform farm-related services and are based in Ulricehamn. We have a close collaboration with the Sjuhärad Farming Society, where research and experimental activities are carried out as well as training through the Strömma Naturbrukcentrum. The head office is at the Rural Advisory Center in Länghem, a few miles from Borås. We offer a fantastic work environment with committed colleagues and short decision-making paths. Qualifications You need to have a driver's license and access to a car and be trained as an agronomist, land master or equivalent. Welcome with your application!

job_title: Försöksassistent
job_description: Department of Land and Environment Do you want to be part of the search for knowledge about how we produce food in the best sustainable way, with minimized negative environmental impact? Do you want varied work in an agricultural environment? Before 2025, we have several new exciting attempts where we need the help of interested seasonal staff. We have the greatest need during the period April-September. If you can only work part of this period, you are still welcome to apply. About the job The tasks are above all to help with tasks that occur in our plant cultivation experiments, such as weighing seed and fertilizer, measuring experimental areas, carrying out various agricultural measures, carrying out soil sampling and crop, i.a. frequent measurements of gas emissions. There is also some work with sample handling, packaging of samples and maintenance of equipment. During intensive periods in crop cultivation, some evening work may be relevant. Your background We are looking for you who are interested in experimental activities in agricultural crop cultivation and who preferably have some form of education in agriculture. Experience of driving tractors, agricultural implements, drones and various measuring equipment is advantageous. The work requires accuracy and the ability to understand both oral and written instructions in Swedish. B driving license is a requirement. In the selection, great importance was attached to the applicant's personal suitability. About usLanna research station outside Skara conducts field experiments for researchers within SLU and for other actors. The business has a strong focus on precision farming, plant nutrition and stable manure and has many long-term trials. Here there are unique facilities for measuring leaching and climate gases and several newly purchased special machines for advanced plant cultivation trials.  Within the trial operations at Lanna, two people work full-time and 1-2 seasonal employees with the field operations. There is also a part-time research leader and a couple of employees in agricultural operations. The Lanna research station is part of the Department of Soil and Environment, which is a leading soil science center, both nationally and internationally. We research the properties and basic functions of the soil, as well as study how environmental and climate changes affect the soil. Through research, environmental analysis and education, we contribute knowledge about future sustainable land use and develop new solutions as a basis for decisions in agriculture and forestry, as well as urban environments. The work environment at the department is international and we have approx. 100 employees. We form part of SLU's Land, Water and Environment Center (MVM center), with close contacts to environmental analysis and research on e.g. water, cycle and bioenergy. The business contributes to meeting national environmental and climate goals and the UN's global sustainability goals. The department is located at Campus Ultuna in Uppsala and at Skara. Read more about the department here (https://www.slu.se/mark). Read more about our benefits and what it's like to work at SLU at https://www.slu.se/om-slu/jobba-pa -slu/Location: Lanna, trial cultivation outside Lidköping Form of employment: Temporary employment approx. 6 months Scope: 60% - 100% Access: 2025-04-01 or according to agreement. Application: Welcome with your application via the application button below no later than 2025-01-31. Union contact persons: https://internt.slu.se/min-anstallning/facket/kontaktpersons/Sveriges lantbruksuniversitet (SLU) has a key role in the development of sustainable living, founded in science and education. Through our focus on the interplay between humans, animals and ecosystems and a responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable social development and good living conditions on our planet. The main locations are Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, but operations are also carried out at research stations, experimental parks and educational locations throughout the country. SLU has roughly 3,000 employees, 5,000 students and research students and a turnover of over three billion kroner. The university invests in attractive environments on its campus areas. We work for an equal and inclusive work environment where open conversations between people with different experiences lay the foundation for science, creativity and development. We therefore welcome people with different backgrounds and perspectives to apply for the current position.

job_title: Plant cultivation adviser to the Housekeeping Society Kalmar Kronoberg Blekinge
job_description: About the position We are looking for a horticulture advisor for our office in Kalmar. We have an existing customer group on Öland where the majority have animal production with forage farming, therefore it is important that you have good competence in crop rotation and maize. You will have your own customer responsibility for these customers but also work closely with your plant cultivation advisor colleagues at the company. Within Hushållningsällskapet Kalmar Kronoberg Blekinge, there are also advisers with expertise in construction, agricultural economics, accounting, environment, water and forestry. You will help customers with plant cultivation planning, field advice, EU support and financial follow-up of crops. It also includes writing advisor letters. You are expected to get involved in our customer development and come up with creative ideas on how our services can be developed to meet our customers' needs. It is advantageous if you have knowledge of irrigation of agricultural crops or are knowledgeable in machine costs. About you You need have a strong personal interest in crop cultivation, including cereals, fodder, maize and oilseeds. In order to thrive in this role, you must also have an understanding of the need for cost-effective food production. Important personal qualities are drive, pedagogy and communication. You need to be communicative both with our customers and with your colleagues. It is a strength if you are unprestigious and generous in sharing your experiences and skills. It is also a strength if you are open to testing new ways of working and new innovations in crop cultivation. We place great emphasis on personal qualities. Qualifications We are looking for you who are a qualified soil plant agronomist or farm manager, or equivalent. Alternatively, you who have worked with crop cultivation for a long professional life and have solid experience in this. B driving license is a requirement, as well as very good knowledge of Swedish, both spoken and written. We offer With us you get the opportunity to develop the green industries together with other knowledgeable and committed employees. We specialize in plant cultivation consultancy for agricultural companies. We have an independent role that is appreciated by our clients. We have flexible working hours and the possibility to work remotely to a certain extent. We also have a wellness allowance and one wellness hour a week. You get a great opportunity to influence how your working week looks like. At the Housekeeping Society you get the opportunity to develop, your work is characterized by freedom under responsibility while you are involved and contribute to the development of the green sector and a living countryside. Access dates by agreement. The position is a permanent position. Probationary employment of 6 months may be applied. Placement sorter Kalmar. Last application date 2025-01-08. We will process the applications on an ongoing basis. The position may be filled before the application deadline. If you have questions about the position, please contact: Team Manager, Pernilla Mattsson: pernilla.mattsson@hushallningssallskapet.se, 072-351 50 68 Welcome with your application! Hushållningssällskapet Kalmar Kronoberg Blekinge Knowledge for the country's future is our promise. We are one of 15 independent Household Associations with the goal of promoting rural development. The household association is an independent, non-profit organization that works for knowledge, research and development of rural green industries and an increased level of supply in Swedish food. We are a member-led organisation, which means that it is the needs of our members that form the backbone of our business. The Kalmar Kronoberg Blekinge household management company consists of approx. 230 employees who are spread across six different offices and schools. job_title: Researchers in ecosystem services in strip cultivation
job_description: The Department of Bio Systems and Technology Som Jobs It is important to reduce the unilateral cultivation of a few crops in large fields, and instead increase the diversity of crops to benefit biodiversity and increase ecosystem services such as biological control. In addition, a greater variety of cultivated crops is promising to increase the return and/or reduce the dependence on pesticides. In this project we will assess whether strip cultivation, where two or more crops are grown next to each other in strips adapted to the width of modern sowing machines, can strengthen biological control, reduce the use of pesticides and maintain harvests compared to when each crop is grown alone on the field. In addition, we will validate the experiment with trials on farms, where farmers themselves decide the management. We are looking for a motivated person with a few years of experience as a researcher and with the ambition of an academic career, who also has a great interest in developing knowledge about the effect of the strip cultivation on biological Control of pests and the return on economically important agricultural crops. The candidate is expected to investigate what potential strip cultivation in practically applicable care has to mitigate the harvest loss of the pest. This means, among other things, planning a cultivation attempt at the university's experimental station, field work, collaboration with Swedish and international partners and to investigate agricultural acceptance of innovative cultivation systems such as strip cultivation. We attach great importance to personal fitness and are looking for you who have good cooperative ability but also be able to work independently. You are looking for you who have: • Doctorate in biology with a focus on insect ecology and their ecosystem services in diversified cultivation systems, or equivalent • demonstrated research experience in the subjects insect pollination and biological control of pests, insect diversity in legumes and rapeseed and effects of co -cultivation • High skills in statistical processing and handling of ecological data • showed ability to publish research results in international scientifically examined magazines • Excellent knowledge in written and oral communication in English and oral Communication in Swedish • Effective communication skills, a strong work ethic and shown experience in collaborating with stakeholders outside the academy • Granted applications with the Research Council are qualified if you also have: • Experience in international collaborations • Experience in project planning, field work and project management • Experience in supervision T .ex. Students' degree projecting Oss research at the Department of Bio Systems and Technology explores the interaction between land, plants, animals, environment, climate and people in systems for sustainable production of food and renewable raw materials. The department has a broad expertise in agricultural and horticultural science and delivers research-based knowledge in teaching and through active collaboration and dense dialogue with stakeholders. We are currently about 60 employees including researchers, doctoral students and support staff. External web leaf more about our benefits and what it is like to work at SLU at https://www.slu.se/om-su/jobba-pa-slu/placing:alnarpansting form:Stidsvidarest position. SLU may apply probationary employment. Swap: 100%access: April 1, 2025 application: The application must be written in English and contain in) a depiction of scientific interests and justification for why this employment is sought (max one page); ii) Brief project plan (max two pages); iii) Curriculum Vitae including a full publication list, which distinguishes scientifically reviewed articles from other publications. /Contact persons/Swedish University of Agriculture (SLU) has a key role in the development of sustainable life, founded in science and education. Through our focus on the interaction between humans, animals and ecosystems and a responsible use of natural resources, we contribute to sustainable social development and good living conditions on our planet. The main places are Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala, but operations are also conducted at research stations, subject parks and places of education throughout the country. The university is investing in attractive environments in its campus areas. We work for an equal and inclusive work environment where open conversations between people with different experiences lay the foundation for science, creativity and development. We therefore welcome people with different backgrounds and perspectives to apply for the current employment.

job_title: Responsable de pôle installation en agriculture (F/H)
job_description: Description of the entityThe Department of Agriculture and Marine Resources (DARM) is responsible for supporting, implementing, leading, monitoring and adapting regional and European policies in the agricultural sector and forestry, the equine economy, fishing and aquaculture as well as the valorization of land and sea products. It includes 103 agents and is organized into 5 services, a sectoral steering mission European funds FEADER (European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development) / FEAMPA (European Fund for Maritime Affairs, Fisheries and Aquaculture) and an internal control unit.  The challenges for management are: Supporting Norman farmers in the development of their farms and transitions; Better valorize regional forest production; Give new impetus to Normandy fishing and move towards recognized and diversified Normandy aquaculture; Promote agricultural, fishing and aquaculture products; Support professionals in the equine industry and promote this sector of excellence internationally.   Missions Since January 1, 2023, the Region has been responsible for managing aid for setting up in agriculture on its territory. In this context, the challenge for the community is therefore to support young people wishing to settle in Normandy with the aim of ensuring the maintenance of the number of agricultural and equine businesses in its territory and allowing generational renewal. As part of its new 2023-2027 program, the Region has set itself the objective of creating 450 installations per year in Normandy.  The purpose of this position is to provide local supervision to a team of managers responsible for examining installation assistance files and overseeing regional installation policy.  Currently, nearly 2,300 living files are managed by the installation assistance system center.  Local management Lead and plan the activity of the division: definition of objectives and priorities, adaptation of the team's activities with regard to workloads, in conjunction with its line manager; Monitor the overall activity of the division and monitor the individual activity of the agents of the division; Provide technical and economic expertise in installation assistance files to managers, resolution of complex files; Organize and coordinate the various processes of the division in order to ensure fluidity in the processing of files; Organize the monitoring and implementation of the supervision and control processes of managers’ files; Propose budgetary developments and monitoring (commitments, payments) linked to this policy in connection with the Regional and FEADER budgets; Ensure day-to-day HR management in conjunction with your department manager; Ensure the replacement of the department manager during absence.  Lead the regional policy in favor of the installation in agriculture and the equine sector Design, implement then monitor the regional installation policy and design of the new post-2027 programming (participation in the French Region working group, consultation with the installation professionals in Normandy, etc.) for the benefit of project leaders and the Normandy territory; Organize and lead strategic meetings (regional installation committee in Normandy, meeting of prescribers, etc.); Represent the Region in strategic and field meetings for technical intervention and promotion of regional mechanisms; Provide technical-economic expertise to external requests for installation assistance files, as well as the liveability and viability of the installation projects presented; Monitor the evolution of current programming and its regulatory developments by being proactive in developing, modernizing and simplifying aid systems and their processes; Monitor the evaluation of the devices and its control methods; Design and update internal procedural documents, external documents intended for beneficiaries and partner structures of the installation, writing notes and reports Profile Expected skills Experience and knowledge in the field of entrepreneurship, particularly agricultural and equine, and in particularly the analysis of the resulting economic data;  Managerial experience/skills desired;  Ability to anticipate, prioritize and adapt your own activities and those of your team;  Spirit of rigor and organization, ability to handle complex files;  Availability and listening, sense of negotiation;  Team spirit and mutual aid, kindness; Ability to take initiatives and be proactive;  Responsiveness and ability to decide effectively; Work independently and responsibly on your missions, while knowing how to report to your hierarchy;  Knowledge of the functioning of European EAFRD programs and funds;  Use and design of specific computer applications and use of office tools; Relational skills internally and externally, ability to popularize complex technical elements and to speak in public; Writing skills.   General conditions Internal contacts Within the management with managers, other service managers, the management secretariat, the EAFRD European funds steering mission.   External contacts Project leaders, professional agricultural partners and the paying agency (ASP).  Special constraints Work in offices and in services; Office hours but with irregular rhythm with potential peaks; Possible time constraints outside office hours on an ad hoc basis; Travel throughout Normandy.   Opportunities Joining the Normandy Region means joining a community that listens to its agents, offering in particular a social action system (CNAS membership), a restaurant voucher card (Caen), a concierge service, a prevention plan health at work as well as participation in a certified mutual insurance company and a nearby SNCF train station.  Recruitment conditions Remuneration according to statutory conditions + Compensation scheme. Vacant position to be filled as soon as possible according to the statutory recruitment procedures. The recruitment jury will be held in the second half of January 2025.

job_description: Do you want to help shape the sustainable society of the future? Södertälje municipality is looking for a creative and innovative person for the role of cultivation coordinator/cultivation project manager. The assignment is a temporary position starting no later than January 2025. Here you get the chance to influence how we protect our farmland and promote local food production, all in line with the municipality's goal of becoming climate neutral by 2030. The position is located at the park and landscape unit at the Community Planning Office. In the unit, we are a total of 14 people who work on issues related to park planning, ecosystem services, pollination, cultivation coordination and much more. We enjoy being together very well on the unit and have a kind climate where we care for each other, our differences and where we are happy to cooperate. Among your colleagues at the unit, you will find people with roles such as landscape architect, park engineer, administrator, coordinator and unit manager. We all work together towards the municipality's overall goals in ecological, social and financial sustainability. With us, you have the opportunity to contribute to a truly sustainable society. About the Service As part of the continuous work with sustainability, a municipality-wide cultivation strategy with accompanying action plan has been adopted, with the aim of showing how the municipality, based on its various roles and functions, should promote local cultivation and protect the arable land. As Cultivation Coordinator/Cultivation Project Manager, you will play a key role in implementing and following up on our cultivation strategy. You will lead projects that integrate cultivation into community planning, support professional horticulture and agriculture, and develop recreational and complementary cultivation. Your work will contribute to ensuring long-term sustainable production methods that benefit biodiversity and create sustainable cycles of nutrients and water. Your tasks will include: - Implementation of Strategy: Implement measures according to the cultivation strategy and action plan to achieve the municipality's overall goals. - Coordination: Work cross-sectorally with various committees and companies to ensure effective implementation of the strategy. - Advice and Support: Continue to develop systems for cultivation advice and grants and support professional horticulture and agriculture. - Communication: Inform and inspire citizens and stakeholders about the possibilities for local cultivation. Who are you? We are looking for you who have: - Education and/or experience in agronomy, environmental science, park planning, gardener or similar field in the green industry. - Experience in project management and cross-sector collaboration. - Ability to express yourself well in Swedish, both orally and in writing. - Good knowledge of digital tools. - B driver's license. Meritorious: - Previous work in the public sector or with sustainability issues. - Experience of strategic planning in agriculture or horticulture. - Interest in social sustainability and community development. - Experience of/knowledge of application processes for external funds and grants relevant to the service. Personal characteristics: You are structured, creative, results-oriented and have a strong ability to collaborate and find new innovative solutions. You can easily create contact with other people and are good at communicating both internally and externally. You are passionate about sustainable development and always have the citizens' best interests in mind when you take on projects. We attach great importance to your personal qualities. We offer you You will sit in our modern city hall a stone's throw from the center of Södertälje with good communication options such as buses and commuter trains and with a fantastic view of both the city and the canal. We sit in an open office landscape, but also offer the possibility of remote work for a certain part of your working time. We apply annual working hours, which means that you have a certain flexibility in how you allocate your working hours. The position is a temporary position until and including 15-01-2026. Each day passes approx 6,000 people to their jobs in Södertälje municipality. We have many different roles with us and want to offer you a meaningful job where you get the opportunity to contribute to society while feeling joy. As an employee with us, you get the opportunity to develop and make a real impression. As an employee of Södertälje municipality, you are offered, among other things, safe employment conditions, a generous wellness allowance and the opportunity to exchange the holiday allowance for extra days off. Within certain businesses, there is also the possibility of some flexibility regarding working hours and working methods. We have a large range of training and skills-enhancing efforts for you as an employee. For more detailed information about our benefits, please read more on our external website: https://www. soder waist. se/admanerWelcome to us! Other Selection and interviews will take place continuously during the application period. Södertälje municipality works with competence-based recruitment methodology with the aim of countering discrimination and promote diversity in the workplace. Employment with us can mean placement in a security class. A security check with a register check according to the Security Protection Act (2018:585) may therefore be carried out before a decision on employment. Swedish citizenship is required for some of our duties in security class. We are happy to receive calls from you who are interested in the job, but we refuse you who sell advertisements and recruitment services.

job_title: Work with plant protection - three services in our socially important business
job_description: The Swedish Agency for Agriculture exists to promote increased and sustainable food production and good animal welfare throughout Sweden. We contribute to a living countryside. About 1,750 people work with us. The head office is in Jönköping, but we also have large regional operations. Read more about what it's like to work at Jordbruksverket on our website: www. the agricultural agency. se/jobbahososs As an advisor in plant protection, you will be part of the plant protection center in Skara, which is part of the environment and climate knowledge hub and works to actively influence and contribute to sustainable plant protection and a competitive, profitable and increased food production. We work in teams and help each other with the tasks that need to be carried out. The colleagues in the environment and climate knowledge hub are mainly located regionally at the Swedish Agency for Agriculture's three advisory units. This position is located at the plant protection advisory unit, which includes the plant protection centre. At the plant control unit, where the administrative positions are located, we are responsible for managing, among other things the rules for seed and against plant pests. This means everything from EU and international work, to national regulations and decisions, together with a lot of guidance, information and preparedness work. At the unit, we are 18 employees divided into two teams. We work both directly with industry players, industry organizations and in collaboration with the government office and other member states. JOB TASKS Do you have a good knowledge of the challenges of plant cultivation and want to work for robust and sustainable plant protection? Do you want to contribute to us being able to continue growing crops for feed and food in Sweden even in the event of social disturbances and in a changed climate? Then you can become one of our new colleagues! The Swedish Agency for Agriculture has an important task in both working with preventive plant protection and combating plant pests that are already present here, partly through regulations and partly through advice and skills development. We are now advertising three positions with the following tasks: 1. Advisor crop protection, agriculture - Skara• compile and convey Swedish and international experiences and results in the field of plant protection to the consultancy, • support the consultancy with increased competence through newsletters, control recommendations, courses, field trips and conferences, • follow the development of plant pests during the season within the Swedish Agency for Agriculture's forecasting activities for various pests, • increase awareness of difficult-to-control weeds and spread knowledge about sustainable cultivation systems, • be an important part of various projects within preparedness to ensure that we can maintain Swedish food production2. Plant pest manager - Jönköping/Landskrona• guide and inform about our rules against quarantine pests, • strengthen our preparedness for and manage possible outbreaks, • contribute to planning and developing our inventory of quarantine pests. Together with the colleagues at the plant regulation unit, you protect Sweden against the introduction of new plant pests. The work involves a mixture of situations that requires quick responses and planned work with processes based on scouting and reflection. 3. Manager robust crop cultivation - Jönköping• what abilities are needed to run the business, • what vulnerabilities exist and • what we need to do to increase our ability. Together with colleagues, you contribute to making our socially important business more robust with rules and guidance both on seed and combating plant pests. This is to reduce our vulnerability and strengthen our preparedness to face new as well as ongoing challenges. QUALIFICATIONSWe are looking for you who have an academic education as an agronomist, hortologist, farm manager, horticultural engineer or equivalent and a good knowledge of crop cultivation in Sweden. You need a good ability to express yourself verbally and in writing, in both Swedish and English to be successful in the role of administrator or advisor. The roles have different qualifying requirements, where the personal abilities we are looking for may differ, depending on the nature of the role and task. The following paragraphs clarify which requirements are specifically aimed at a particular service. 1. For advisers in crop protection, in addition to the requirements above, you need to have experience of working as a plant cultivation adviser under Nordic conditions and good knowledge of plant pests and integrated plant protection in agricultural crops. You are structured and used to planning your work, are confident in your professional role and find solutions to get ahead even in uncertain contexts. You stay up-to-date by monitoring the world around you and find it easy to put forward your case and win respect. 2. For plant pest manager, you need to be structured, analytical and communicative. It is advantageous to have knowledge of plant pests, gardening, plant cultivation or forests in Nordic conditions, and if you have experience of government work. 3. For manager of robust crop cultivation, we are looking for you who is structured, stable and has an easy time collaborating and communicating with others, both customers and other actors. You have previous experience of government work and we would like you to have experience of work in civil defence. OTHER Location of the services is presented below:1. Plant protection advisers are primarily located in Skara, but Linköping can also be an option. 2. Pest control officers are based in Jönköping or Landskrona. 3. Handler robust crop cultivation is located in Jönköping. For all three positions, the opportunity to work part of the working time remotely is offered. Do you have questions about any of the services? 1. For plant protection advisers, contact Anna Larsson or Anders Arvidsson. 2. For plant pest managers, contact Carin Bunnvik. 3. For managers robust plant cultivation, contact Carin Bunnvik or Klara Ekengard. For us, it is important that all skills in the labor market are utilized. We welcome all applicants and strive for diversity. We normally apply a 6-month trial period. Before the recruitment work, we have taken a position on recruitment channels and marketing. We therefore do not want to be contacted by advertising vendors or recruitment companies.

testCases.name: test_case_19
testCases.input: Are there any open roles in Sweden for professionals responsible for coordinating farm personnel, field activities, and agricultural resources?
testCases.actualOutput:
Based on the retrieved context from the database, there are several open roles in Sweden that involve the coordination of farm personnel, field activities, and agricultural resources. 

Here are the positions matching your request:

### 1. **Lantbrukare med huvudansvar för jordbruk och djurhållning (Stensjö village)**
*   **Focus:** This position involves primary responsibility for agriculture and animal husbandry at the Stensjö cultural reserve.
*   **Key Responsibilities:**
    *   Coordinating and performing ongoing work within the farm (organic orientation).
    *   Supervising seasonal workers during the growing season.
    *   Participation in management councils and contacts with the County Administrative Board regarding the cultural reserve.
    *   Administrative tasks including EU applications, reporting, and registration using programs like Dataväxt and Växa Sverige.
*   **Requirements:** Documented experience in crop cultivation and animal husbandry, experience in work management, and a B driving license (BE is a merit).

### 2. **Distriktssäljare i Skåne (DeLaval)**
*   **Focus:** This role involves sales, advice, and planning facilities and systems for farmers.
*   **Key Responsibilities:**
    *   Coordinating and project managing work for builders, authorities, and advisory bodies.
    *   Acting as support for customers in planning facilities and systems.
*   **Requirements:** Knowledge of Swedish agriculture, experience in sales or consultancy, and experience in project management.

### 3. **Expert/project manager in milk for sustainable animal production (RISE)**
*   **Focus:** Collecting and coordinating different competencies in milk production to contribute to knowledge transfer.
*   **Key Responsibilities:**
    *   Gathering and coordinating experts, industry partners, and RISE competencies.
    *   Identifying the knowledge needs of animal producers and developing advisory methods.
    *   Interdisciplinary work regarding animal health, breeding, feed, and production economics.
*   **Requirements:** University-level education (agronomist, veterinarian, or farm manager), experience with the milk production process, and experience working in national/international projects.

### 4. **Jordbruksverket – Seasonal positions at Plant Protection Centers**
*   **Focus:** Forecasting and warning activities regarding plant pests and diseases.
*   **Key Responsibilities:**
    *   Monitoring and sampling of plant pests in fields across various agricultural crops (straw, oilseeds, legumes, vegetables, fruit).
    *   Compiling results and assisting in information meetings for advisors and farmers.
    *   Collaborating as part of a team at regional centers in Kalmar, Skara, Linköping, Uppsala, and Landskrona.
*   **Requirements:** Experience in agriculture or the green sector (crop cultivation), structured approach to work, and ability to collaborate within a team.

### 5. **Byggrådgivare (Construction Consultant) – Hushållningssällskapet**
*   **Focus:** Construction consultancy for farmers and rural businesses.
*   **Key Responsibilities:**
    *   Customer contact, construction management, and site visits.
    *   Administrative tasks from sales and project management to invoicing.
    *   Leading projects and collaborating with an experienced construction team.
*   **Requirements:** Structured, service-oriented with a drive for teamwork; knowledge of stable environment and animal flows is considered a merit.

JobDescription: The county board's approximately 300 employees work as the government's representative at regional level. Our mission is to develop the county and work to ensure that the national political goals have an impact in the county. The unit has overall responsibility for rural issues and is responsible for the agricultural and rural focus in the cross-sector collaboration at the County Board. The county. This includes, among other things, counseling and skills-enhancing activities aimed at the county's farmers. Our current pet consultant is now retiring and we are therefore looking for her successor who wants to work with skills development for the county's farmers with a focus on the farm's animal husbandry. Job duties You will be part of a group that works with planning, implementing and leading skills development within the common agricultural policy in the form of advice, courses and information to farmers. The work entails partly independently carrying out competence-enhancing initiatives such as courses, counseling and farm meetings with exchange of experience and partly coordinating other actors that the county administrative board has procured for various activities. You write applications for project funds and, together with colleagues, carry out the procurement of competence development efforts. The work includes financial accounting and reporting of measures taken. You collaborate with industry actors and organizations and have close cooperation with other county administrative boards as well as with various functions at our county administrative board. You may be part of cross-sectoral groups where you need to be able to combine your expertise with a holistic perspective. You participate in the work of responding to referrals and contributing with the perspective of agriculture on various issues. Your work is independent and requires you to be self-motivated, results-oriented and good at collaborating and creating relationships. You are sensitive to the needs of different clients. JobTitle: Expert/project manager in milk for sustainable animal production
JobDescription: Do you have knowledge of and experience in milk production? Do you want to work with the sustainable milk production of the future together with companies and the consultancy in the agricultural and animal sector? Then this could be a service for you! About us The government wishes to strengthen competitiveness in animal production for food by ensuring that the newest knowledge nationally and internationally is useful for Swedish producers. Knowledge hub animal production is a new unit within RISE that we are building together with experts in the field and who have competence in knowledge transfer, advice and communication. Together with the actors, we will identify the needs of animal production and develop models and advisory methods, which will put the knowledge to use by the farmer. The knowledge hub should not conduct research or advice itself, but be a link between the research and the advice and should collect knowledge from different areas and make it useful for advisory companies and the farmers. About the role We are now expanding our team with another expert in the field of milk production. As an expert in our team, you get the opportunity to work with acquisition, compilation and transfer of knowledge regarding milk production, animal health and welfare, breeding, feed, milk quality, new technology and entrepreneurship. This is for a future sustainable Swedish animal production, which contributes to good animal welfare and working environment, together with good profitability. You will be an important team player in a committed department with high competence and who values ​​working in close collaboration with both colleagues within RISE and with our partners. You will have an important key role where you gather and coordinate different competences in milk production with our experts, industry partners and other RISE competencies, to contribute to knowledge transfer based on the animal producer's current and future needs. The position is located in Uppsala or Lund and involves some travel, therefore a B driving license is a requirement. Who are you? You have an education at at least university level as an agronomist, veterinarian, farm manager or equivalent. You have experience and knowledge of the entire milk production process, i.e. knowledge within i.a. animal health, breeding, feed, production economics and management. We would like you to have experience of working interdisciplinary, as well as working with information delivery and identifying farmers' knowledge needs, in national/international projects. It is advantageous if you have several years of work experience in the field of milk production, information efforts/further training and counseling for agricultural entrepreneurs. As a person, you are focused, committed, driven and good at building relationships with e.g. You work goal-oriented and structured and have a strong ability to quickly absorb information and events. Your way of thinking is strategic and you have a good overall view. You are proactive and systematic in your way of working and like to think new things. Very good knowledge of Swedish and English, both spoken and written, is a requirement. What do we offer you? With us at RISE, you will get to work with an incredibly broad and exciting business. You will be part of a network of experts where you will be given the opportunity to exchange experience and develop skills as well as a valuable sounding board. You will collaborate with our researchers and experts in agricultural production. The culture is characterized by a positive spirit where everything is possible and where we work focused towards our common goals. You will work in a dynamic environment that gives you development opportunities both professionally and personally. At RISE, we want you to succeed and feel good, because when you succeed, you contribute to a sustainable future. Do you want to know more? Welcome to contact Jørgen Korning, Head of Unit, 070-313 6996. The deadline for applications is 10 November 2024. Interviews will take place continuously during and after the application period. Our union representatives are: Ingemar Petermann, SACO 010-2284122 and Linda Ikatti, 010-516 51 61. Calls from external recruitment companies and sellers are kindly avoided as we are subject to the Public Procurement Act.

JobTitle: Jordbruksverket söker säsongsanställda till växtskyddscentralerna!
JobDescription: The Swedish Agency for Agriculture exists to promote increased and sustainable food production and good animal welfare throughout Sweden. We contribute to a living countryside. About 1,850 people work with us. The head office is in Jönköping, but we also have large regional operations. We work actively to ensure that our employees are sustainable and happy at work! We invest long-term in our employees and want them to develop together with us! We offer a good working environment with generous benefits with up to 35 vacation days, wellness allowance and wellness time. In a large part of our employment, we offer flexible working hours, the opportunity to work mobile and work part of the working time remotely. Read more about what it's like to work at the Swedish Agricultural Agency on our website: www.jordbruksverket.se/jobbahosossARBETSUPPGIFTERNu we are looking for you who want to combine your interest in plant protection with an educational and fun job during the spring and summer semesters!The work at the plant protection centers mainly involves recurring gradations of plant pests in fields during the season, which is part of our forecasting and warning activities. The work may also include various sampling and inventories in the field for specific pests and resistance surveys. In the office and lab, you will work with compilation of results and disease and insect diagnostics. You may also have the opportunity to participate in field walks and information meetings for advisors and farmers. The agricultural crops we work with are straw, oilseeds, legumes, potatoes, corn and sugar beet. In fruit and berries, we focus mostly on apples and strawberries, and for outdoor vegetables we are mostly out in the largest crop groups; cabbage, carrots and onions. The plant protection centers are located in different parts of the country and are part of the advisory unit's work. We are looking for seasonal employees for the offices in Kalmar, Skara, Linköping, Uppsala and Landskrona. The work within Greppa Näringen mainly involves measuring nitrogen uptake in fields in southern Sweden and calculations and compilation of results. The goal is to provide a decision-making basis for adapted fertilization. Here is our need for the 2025 season: Plant Protection Center Landskrona, agriculture1-2 people, approximately 1 April to 31 October, full-time1-2 people, approximately 1 June to 31 August, full-time Plant Protection Center Landskrona, garden (free-range vegetables , fruit, berries)1 person, approximately April 1 to September 30, full-time1 person, approximately June 1 to August 31, full-time Plant Protection Center Kalmar, agriculture1 person, approximately April 1 to October 31, full-time1 person, approximately June 1 to August 31, full-time Plant Protection Center Skara, agriculture1 person, approximately May 1 to August 15, full-time1 person, approximately June 1 to August 15, full-time Plant Protection Center Linköping, agriculture1-2 people, approximately April 1 to October 15, full-time Plant Protection Center Uppsala, agriculture1 person, approx. 1 March to 30 September, full-time1 person, approx. 1 May to 15 August, full-timeGreppa Näringen, Landskrona1 person, approx. 1 April to 18 June, 50% Please read more about the plant protection centers at www.jordbruksverket.se/ plants/cultivation/plant protection/currently from the plant protection centers. QUALIFICATIONSWe are looking for you who have work experience connected to agriculture or the green sector, mainly in crop cultivation or professional horticulture. You get to the fields by car, therefore a B driver's license is a requirement. The work requires that you can understand and express yourself well in spoken and written Swedish. It is advantageous if you attend or have completed a post-secondary green education, which we judge to be relevant, or if you have previous experience from having worked at a plant protection centre. We also see it as meritorious if you have knowledge of diseases and plant pests under Nordic conditions and experience monitoring these in the field. You are a structured person who takes responsibility for your task and completes what you start. You are flexible and collaborative, and adapt to find win-win solutions for the whole team. Welcome with your application. Preferably as soon as possible because we interview and make the selection continuously! However, final information will be given after the application period has expired. OTHER Locations are Landskrona, Kalmar, Skara, Linköping and Uppsala. Fill in the questions as thoroughly as you can, as applications with missing or incomplete answers are not considered to the same extent as applications with detailed answers. A realistic answer regarding location and possible work period is important as we make an initial selection based on these criteria. JobTitle: Lantbrukare med huvudansvar för jordbruk och djurhållning
JobDescription: Tasks: We now need to supplement the workforce with you who want to contribute to the development of the cultural reserve Stensjö village. It is a unique opportunity to, together with colleagues on site and with the support of management advice and external expertise, participate in the development work and work towards the cultural-historical target image. During the changes of the seasons, you will contribute to recreating the experience of old-time small farms in the Småland forest region. The position involves primary responsibility for agriculture and animal husbandry in a landscape characterized by natural grazing, mowing fields, small fields and large forest areas. All cultivation is organic. You must be prepared to take on managerial responsibilities. The permanent staff at the farm consists of four people with different areas of responsibility (agriculture, forestry, garden, landscape), one of whom is site manager with overall responsibility for the property. During the growing season, the workforce is supplemented by one to two seasonal workers. The animal supervision on the weekends rotates between the staff so that work takes place according to schedule every third to fourth weekend. Common, ongoing work tasks consist of all tasks occurring within a farm with an ecological orientation and a focus on cultural-historical landscape care. An important task is to continuously document the work that is done. Passing on knowledge of the uniqueness of Stensjö village to visitors and groups is also part of the work. Participation in management councils and ongoing contacts with the County Administrative Board regarding issues relating to the cultural reserve are included, as well as administrative work and authority contacts related to the duties, such as EU and other applications, reporting and registration. Programs used at Stensjö include Dataväxt, Växa Sverige, CDB, Elitlamm etc. About Stensjö village Stensjö village comprises 576 hectares of which 14 hectares are arable, 81 hectares of pasture, 417 hectares of forest and 44 hectares of impediment. The large contiguous areas with natural pastures are distinctive for Stensjö village. A typical feature is the kilometre-long hedgerows that enclose holdings, pastures and cattle lanes. Small fields, mowing fields, pastures and open fields with forest grazing characterize the landscape. The village's great importance lies in the fact that houses and property form a unit that is original. Residential houses and outbuildings, a total of about 50 in number, are gathered in a cluster village, which was common in many places in Småland before legal transfer was carried out in the 19th century. In the village there are about fifteen cows and a bull of the red kulla breed as well as about 30 Helsingo sheep, some pigs and chickens. During the summer months, hired cows walk in the forest pastures. The field cultivation consists of paddy, potatoes and cultivated crops, mainly older cereals but also flax. The land has been cultivated organically since the Vitterhetsakademien took over the property in the 1960s. Since 2020, Stensjö village is a cultural reserve. The management plan aims to show Stensjö as it looked at the turn of the century in 1900. The land types that existed at that time should be well represented in the form of pastures, fodder dikes, gardens, ancient fields with cereal crops, natural hay fields and forest pastures. Long-term work is underway where the management plan is the guiding principle with the aim of recreating an older land use. Stensjö village is to be developed into a knowledge and development center for historic landscape use. The management plan can be found on the website under the Management plan and documents tab. To support the work, there is a management council that meets at Stensjö twice a year. The maintenance council consists of 5-7 people with experience in practical landscape and garden maintenance and building maintenance, as well as representatives for research in relevant areas. Administrative support such as finance, communication etc. can be found at the Vitterhetsakademien's office in Stockholm. Qualifications Requirements for the position You must have documented, solid experience in crop cultivation and animal husbandry Ability to work both independently and together with others Good verbal and written communication skills in Swedish Experience in administration and authority contacts regarding farm support, animal husbandry, EU applications etc. Driving license BMeritandEducation in agriculture and animal husbandryEducation/experience in organic farming with crop rotations Experience of work management Education/experience of: Landscape care with a cultural-historical focus, scythes Work with horses Forestry with clear cutting methods Machine maintenance Building care/property care with an antiquarian focus Experience of museum operations and outward-looking, public activities Basic interest and knowledge of small farms; nature, history and culture, and preferably more specifically about Småland's conditions Driving license BEChainsaw driving license A and BHunting licensePersonal characteristicsWe attach great importance to personal suitability. You can work independently and intensively when required, but also be a good colleague and partner with Stensjö's best interests at heart in all internal and external contexts. You have a great sense of responsibility and can flexibly change between the various tasks. Employment and other information about the work The position is a permanent, full-time position that begins with a six-month probationary period. The work involves scheduled working hours, which includes work on evenings, weekends and public holidays. The academy applies individual salary setting. The workplace is Stensjö village, 10 km north of Oskarshamn. There is an opportunity to live in Stensjö village. The Vitterhetsakademien's office is in Stockholm. Support functions such as finances, administration, communication, IT support, archives, etc. is there. The property manager, who is the immediate manager, has his main place of work in Stockholm but is on site in Stensjö village several times a year. In between, meetings and contact take place via Teams and telephone. Collaboration and meetings with colleagues at the other cultural properties take place regularly, including in connection with joint property meetings twice a year. The members of the Vitterhetsakademie have a great interest in the cultural properties and many regularly visit Stensjö village. There is guest accommodation for them at each cultural property, which enables overnight stays.
